# Calcul des variances des fPC1{.tabset}

Après calcul des variances des fPC1, rangées par ordre décroissante, 
on se rend compte que le dju_refroi et le taux de possession de chat ont des variances très élevées et donc risque de oeser beaucoup dans le modèle GSCA. **La standardisation des variables est donc nécessaire.**

# Interprétation des fPC1{.tabset}

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# fonction pour extraire plus d'une composante fonctionelle

func_data <- function(data, Nb.Base, ncomp){

data <- data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(annee = annee %>% factor, region = region %>%  factor)

# Paramètres
Temps      <- levels(data$annee)
NbTemps    <- length(Temps)
VarName    <- colnames(data)[-c(1:2)]
NbVar      <- length(VarName)
Regions    <- levels(data$region)
NbRegions  <- length(Regions)
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "grey", "red"))

# Transformation des variables en matrice
mat_tmps_reg <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) as.matrix(reshape2:::dcast(data, annee  ~ region, value.var = VarName[p])[, -1]))

# transformation en objet fonctionnel
# Base B-spline
spline.basis <- fda::create.bspline.basis(rangeval = c(0, 1), nbasis = Nb.Base, norder = 3)
# plot(spline.basis, lty = 1, lwd = 2, main = "Base de B-splines", xlab = 'Temps')
# Projection des données dans la base
data.amc.fd <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) {
  mat <- mat_tmps_reg[[p]]
  mat <- cbind(mat, annee = 2012:2024)
  mat <- na.omit(mat)
  Temps <- levels(as.factor(mat[, "annee"]))
  NbTemps    <- length(Temps)
  mat <- mat[,-which(colnames(mat) == "annee")]
  Time.01      <- seq(0, 1, length.out = NbTemps)
  fda::smooth.basis(Time.01, mat, spline.basis)$fd})

# fcpa
fPCA.amc <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) fda::pca.fd(data.amc.fd[[p]], nharm = ncomp, centerfns = TRUE))
names(fPCA.amc) <- VarName
df <- data.frame(col1 = rep(NA,12))
for (j in 1:NbVar){
  d <- as.data.frame(fPCA.amc[[j]]$scores)
  colnames(d) <- paste0(VarName[j], "_fPC", 1:ncol(d))
  df <- cbind.data.frame(df, d)
}
df <- df[,-1]
rownames(df) <- c("Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes", "Bourgogne-Franche-Comte", "Bretagne",               
"Centre-Val de Loire", "Grand Est", "Hauts-de-France", "IDF", "Normandie",               "Nouvelle-Aquitaine", "Occitanie", "PACA", "Pays de la Loire")
return(list(df, fPCA.amc))
}

```

## log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G

- fPC1 (95.7 %): différence régions qui consomment beaucoup de C3G tout le temps (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) VS régions qui en consomment peu tous le temps (Pays de la Loire)
- fPC2 (2.8%): changement à partir de 2020 (covid), des régions consomment plus cette année là (IDF), ou après (Normandie, Auvergne Rhône Alpes)
- les scores fonctionnels n'ont pas l'air normalement distribués, elles semblent left skewed (surtout fPC1): **à réfléchir pour le bootstrap quelle autre loi peut convenir, peut-être faire des tests d'adéquation à une loi.**

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

cols <- c("IDF" = "#FFD700", 
          "Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes" = "#FB6A4A", "PACA" = "#CB181D", 
          "Nouvelle-Aquitaine" = "#FD8D3C", "Occitanie" = "#D94701",
          "Centre-Val de Loire" = "#9ECAE1", "Pays de la Loire" = "#6BAED6",
          "Normandie" = "#3182BD", "Bretagne" = "#08519C", 
          "Bourgogne-Franche-Comte" = "#74C476", "Grand Est" = "#31A354", 
          "Hauts-de-France" = "#006D2C")

plot_fpca_gg <- function(pca_fd_obj, harm = 1, xlab = "Temps", title = NULL) {
  
  # Grille de temps
  t_grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
  # Moyenne
  mean_vals <- fda::eval.fd(t_grid, pca_fd_obj$meanfd)
  # Fonction propre (harm-ième)
  harmfd   <- pca_fd_obj$harmonics[harm]
  harm_vals <- fda::eval.fd(t_grid, harmfd)
  # Variance expliquée
  varprop <- round(pca_fd_obj$varprop[harm] * 100, 1)
  # Amplitude de perturbation (comme plot.pca.fd)
  score_sd <- sqrt(pca_fd_obj$values[harm])
  
  df <- data.frame(
    t     = t_grid,
    mean  = mean_vals[, 1],
    plus  = mean_vals[, 1] + score_sd * harm_vals[, 1],
    minus = mean_vals[, 1] - score_sd * harm_vals[, 1]
  )
  
  if (is.null(title)) title <- paste0("fPC", harm, " (", varprop, "% var. exp.)")
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = t)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = mean), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = plus), shape = 3, color = "black") +
    geom_line(aes(y = minus), color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = "") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 1, length.out = 13),
      label = as.character(2012:2024)
      )+
    theme_bw()+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank())
}

plot_comp_func <- function(data, variable){
g1 <- dat %>% 
  dplyr::select(region, annee, variable) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!c("region", "annee"), names_to = "Var",
                      values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = annee, y = value, col = region))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line(show.legend = FALSE)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(color = "Région",
       title = variable)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2012, 2024, by = 1),
                     minor_breaks = seq(2012, 2024, by = 1))+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.6, colour = "black", size = 6), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6), 
        legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.spacing = unit(0.5, "cm"),        
        legend.key.height = unit(0.1, "cm"),   
        legend.key.width = unit(0.1, "cm"),    
        legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm") 
        )+
  scale_color_manual(values = cols)


# Utilisation
p1 <- plot_fpca_gg(data[[2]][[variable]], harm = 1, xlab = "Temps")
p2 <- plot_fpca_gg(data[[2]][[variable]], harm = 2, xlab = "Temps")


p3 <- data[[1]] %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC1")]], 
             y = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC2")]]))+
  geom_text(aes(label = rownames(data[[1]])), size = 2.3)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "fPC1", y = "fPC2")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 6))

p4 <- data[[1]] %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC1")]]))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "gold", color = "black", alpha = .5)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Distribution fPC1")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6))

p5 <- data[[1]] %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC2")]]))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "gold", color = "black", alpha = .5)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Distribution fPC2")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6))


combined <- g1 + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5
return(combined)
}

plot_comp_func(data = dat.func_EHPAD_C3G, variable = "log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G")

```

## log_AMC_EHPAD_FQ

- fPC1: diff moyenne, le PACA consomme beaucoup de FQ, IDF, bretagne et pays de la loire et centre val de loire consomment peu tout le temps
- fPC2: sont bien classées les régions qui consomment de plus en plus de FQ en EHPAD à partir du covid (Hauts-de-France, Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes).
- fPC1 est symétriquement distribuée, fPC2 semble left skewed.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

plot_comp_func(data = dat.func_EHPAD_FQ, variable = "log_AMC_EHPAD_FQ")

```
